projected.source: Open-Meteo Climate API (CMIP6 HighResMIP models), daily temperature_2m_max

sentences.text: At this address, days with an air temperature high of 90°F or more averaged 0.2 days a year in the 2000s and 0.6 days a year in 2016 to 2025, the last 10 years.
The trend test says there is no clear trend yet, so the record does not show a direction.
Climate models project a change of about +8.9 days a year at or above 90°F air temperature, with models ranging from +5.7 to +22.7 days a year.
The models disagree with each other, which is why we show the range across models and not a single answer.
These projections describe a typical year in 2041 to 2050, on climate-model grids of about 20–50 km, downscaled by Open-Meteo to about 10 km, and are not a forecast of any single year.
The models follow a high-emissions path, and the past record has too few years, 26, to tell a trend from natural variation.

past-air-hot-days.title: Days with an air temperature high of 90°F or more
past-air-hot-days.origin: Open-Meteo historical weather archive (ERA5 reanalysis), daily, 2000 to 2025. Counted from the daily record at this address.
past-air-hot-days.text: Days with an air temperature high of 90°F or more, 2000 to 2025. 2000s: 0.2 days a year on average (2 days in 10 years); 2016 to 2025 (the last 10 years): 0.6 days a year on average (6 days in 10 years). Trend test (Mann-Kendall with Sen slope, one value per year; a trend counts only if p is under 0.05). Result: no clear trend yet.

future-hot-days.title: Days per year with an air-temperature high of 90°F or more, in climate models
future-hot-days.origin: Open-Meteo Climate API (CMIP6 HighResMIP models), daily temperature_2m_max. 7 of 7 CMIP6 HighResMIP models had data for this point.
future-hot-days.text: The climate models' own change in days a year at or above 90°F (air temperature, not feels-like), 7 models. Climate models: 1.1/yr (2001 to 2020, models) to 10/yr (2041 to 2050), about +8.9 days a year. Across models the change ranges from +5.7 to +22.7 days a year. Models range from 0.6 to 3.5 in 2001 to 2020 and from 6.3 to 26.2 in 2041 to 2050.

caveat.title: What the projections are, and are not
caveat.origin: Open-Meteo Climate API; CMIP6 HighResMIP climate models
caveat.text: Climate models (CMIP6) are physics simulations, not a forecast, so we show their change. These models follow a high-emissions path (as close to RCP8.5 as CMIP6 gets). We show how much they say it changes, not their raw level. The models run on climate-model grids of about 20–50 km, downscaled by Open-Meteo to about 10 km, and they disagree, so the range across models is shown. They describe how often hot days could occur in a typical year of 2041 to 2050, not what any single year or day will do. A trend in the past record is reported only when a statistical test gives p under 0.05; otherwise the record says "no clear trend yet", which means the 26 years are too few or too variable to tell.
